A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, equations, tables, plots, and Appendices A–D support comparison; text extraction was supplemented by visual inspection.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original noisy 2-XOR experiments, with test errors from sample-size and dimension sweeps in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: Section 5 reports original noisy 2-XOR experiments in Figures 1a–1b, including updated errors, additional dimension settings, and fitted trends.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same fully connected ReLU architecture, symmetric initialization, fixed output weights, logistic loss, and gradient-descent updates. Changes to analytical neighborhoods and proof arguments do not change the training procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate noisy 2-XOR binary classification through sample-size and input-dimension sweeps. The expanded dimension grid remains within the existing sensitivity scenario and dataset family.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparators: Ji and Telgarsky, Lei et al., Chen et al., and Taheri et al.

E3.justification: At fixed n=64, Figure 1b extends the dimension sweep from d=7–12 to points corresponding to d=6–15. Width 128, 500 iterations, step size 0.1, and evaluation over all 2^d distribution points remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing scaling analyses gain additional dimension settings and explicit linear fits in Figures 1a–1b. These refine the evidence concerning test error versus d^2/n; no new component ablations or distinct robustness studies appear.

E5.justification: Figure 1 newly reports linear-fit estimates: y=0.1428x−0.0199 and y=0.1648x−0.0241, where x=d^2/n. v2 only states an approximate 0.15d^2/n relationship. Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or error bars.

E6.justification: Figure 1a changes errors under the same stated settings: at d=6 and n=28, Table 2's 0.2062 becomes approximately 0.125; at n=20, 0.3063 becomes approximately 0.266. Figure 1b retains the earlier dimension results at plotting precision and adds four points. The broad d^2/n trend remains.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces the Frobenius-norm neighborhood with a spectral-norm neighborhood, changing the domain of supporting lemmas. Lemma 12 adds a condition bounding the perturbed activation matrix. Appendix B revises Theorem 1's induction, and Appendix C replaces Lemma 22's extremizer assertion with a supremum-based derivation. Theorem 3 also changes its bound from L^4(1+γL^2)/(nγ^2) to L^6/(nγ^2), up to logarithmic factors.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction's third contribution replace the refined L^4(1+γL^2)/(nγ^2) guarantee with L^6/(nγ^2), suppressing logarithmic factors. The central claims of optimal sample-size/margin dependence, polynomial depth dependence, and reduced width requirements remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 removes the interpretation that the reference-model analysis extends beyond the NTK regime. The experimental scaling interpretation and the stated limitations concerning SGD, behavior far from initialization, and other architectures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same training hyperparameters, exhaustive distribution evaluation, Google Colab execution, and notebook/repository link. No additional implementation, hardware, timing, or access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 drops the beyond-NTK positioning statement and removes Lemma 19's detailed comparison with earlier linearization bounds. The cited-work set remains unchanged: Lei et al.'s preprint-to-journal update and the corrected Mohri textbook entry are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 moves Lemma 1 and Theorem 2 ahead of the detailed remarks and clarifies the proof roadmap. Additional explanatory transitions appear throughout the appendices, and terminology changes from generalization error to generalization gap. The overall document structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 become side-by-side scatter plots against d^2/n, with fitted lines, legends, and panel captions. This changes the experimental display and removes exact tabulated values. Table 1 retains its structure; other layout changes largely follow text reflow.

improvement.justification: The corrected induction indexing in Appendix B, explicit perturbation condition in Lemma 12, and clearer Section 4.2 roadmap modestly improve theoretical precision and readability. These gains are tempered by reduced numerical transparency when exact tables become plots, particularly where errors change without explanation. The revision does not establish stronger overall theoretical or empirical validation.
